newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle active at $69.00 - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle active at $69.00 - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle Tuesday turned fairly active near midday at $69.00 per cwt, up $2.00 from most of last week's trade, feedlot sources said.
About 38,000 head sold in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area, which brought the week to date figure near 56,000, they said.
An estimated 27,500 head sold in Kansas, which brought weekly movement near 31,500, the sources said.
Further bids at $69.00 were passed by some owners asking $70.00, particularly in Kansas amid ideas that fed cattle prices could see higher prices on strong beef demand.
Beef prices Tuesday were quoted up $2.18 to $2.49 per cwt, with heavyweight choice beef up $2.49 at $105.33, USDA statistics showed.
Heavier-weight choice beef was up $6.08 since prices started climbing last Thursday, the statistics showed.
Beef price advances were powered by strong demand from retailers booking orders for planned advertising features at the end of the month, market sources said.

Fed cattle prices also were underpinned by smaller numbers of cattle on this week's showlists and ideas that packers were short on live inventory, as reflected by active buying so early in the week, they said.
Several feedlot sources Tuesday said they had not expected packers to be in the market until Wednesday.
